english.title: Produce device to interfere with / falsify / alter / destroy / suppress data stored on recording equipment
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) produced a device, namely, **(..SPECIFY OR DESCRIBED THE DEVICE..), designed to

(A)_[interfere with the proper operation of recording equipment fitted to a motor vehicle in compliance with the requirement of the Transport Act 1968]_
(B)_[enable the falsification, alteration, destruction or suppression of data stored in compliance with requirements of Community Rules on recording equipment]_
(C)_[enable the falsification, alteration, destruction or suppression of data stored in compliance with requirements of Community Rules on a driver's card]_
english.legislation: Contrary to section 99ZE(6) and (9) of the Transport Act 1968.

english.notes:
(i) Subsection 99ZE(8) of the Transport Act 1968 provides that a person shall not be liable to be convicted under subsection (6) if he proves to the court that he produced, supplied or installed the device, or provided information to assist a person in producing a device, for use in connection with the enforcement of the provisions of this Part of this Act.
(ii) Subsection 99ZE(10) of the Transport Act 1968 provides that for the purposes of this offence, a person shall be taken to permit an act or omission if he is, or ought reasonably to be, aware of the act or omission, or of it being a likelihood, and takes no steps to prevent it.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale,

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
